# package virtual

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-canbus/virtual"
```

Package virtual is a deterministic in-memory CAN bus for tests and simulation, on every operating system.

A [Bus](#type-bus) has any number of ports; each port is a [canbus.Transport](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus#Transport). All frames, from every port, pass through one ordered delivery queue, so every port observes the same global order. Delivery follows SocketCAN's rules: a frame goes to every other port while the sending port has loopback on (the default) and back to the sender only with receive-own-messages; a port opened without CAN FD neither sends nor receives CAN FD frames, and a port opened without CAN XL ([WithXL](#func-withxl)) neither sends nor receives CAN XL frames.

Faults are injected with a seeded pseudo-random generator, so a run is reproducible for a given seed and order of sends: dropped, duplicated, delayed and corrupted frames, error frames, the interface going down and up, ports closing abruptly, and scripted frames from a simulated node ([Bus.Inject](#func-bus-inject)), including frames that violate the frame rules ([Bus.InjectRaw](#func-bus-injectraw)).

The bus models frame delivery only. There is no arbitration, bit timing, acknowledgement, error confinement, automatic retransmission or electrical behaviour: a corrupted frame is delivered corrupted, where a real bus would reject it by its CRC and retransmit it.

#### func (Bus) InjectRaw

```go
func (b *Bus) InjectRaw(ctx context.Context, f canbus.Frame) error
```

InjectRaw delivers a frame without validating it, to test how receivers handle frames a conforming transport never produces (a classical frame with 9 bytes, an unknown flag, garbage beyond Len).

InjectXL delivers a CAN XL frame to every port opened [WithXL](#func-withxl), as if a node outside this process had sent it. The frame is validated. Faults apply.

#### func (Bus) SetUp

```go
func (b *Bus) SetUp(up bool)
```

SetUp brings the interface up or down. While it is down, Send fails with [canbus.ErrInterfaceDown](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus#ErrInterfaceDown), every port's next Receive returns that error once (as a SocketCAN socket reports ENETDOWN), and no frame is delivered.

### type Config

```go
type Config struct {
	// Name is the interface name ports report and frames carry
	// (default "virtual0").
	Name string
	// Seed seeds the fault generator (default 1).
	Seed int64
	// QueueSize is the capacity of the bus's delivery queue (default
	// 4096). Send blocks while it is full.
	QueueSize int
	// Clock returns the receive timestamp of frames (default time.Now).
	Clock func() time.Time
}
```

Config configures a [Bus](#type-bus).

### type FaultStats

```go
type FaultStats struct {
	Delivered  uint64 `json:"delivered"`
	Dropped    uint64 `json:"dropped"`
	Duplicated uint64 `json:"duplicated"`
	Delayed    uint64 `json:"delayed"`
	Corrupted  uint64 `json:"corrupted"`
}
```

FaultStats reports how many frames were delivered and affected by faults so far.

### type Faults

```go
type Faults struct {
	Drop      float64       // probability a frame is lost
	Duplicate float64       // probability a frame is delivered twice
	Delay     float64       // probability a frame is held for DelayBy
	DelayBy   time.Duration // hold time of a delayed frame; later frames wait behind it (the bus is serial)
	Corrupt   float64       // probability one payload bit is flipped
	// DropNext drops the next n frames regardless of the probabilities.
	DropNext int
}
```

Faults are probabilities and parameters of injected faults. Each frame passing the delivery queue draws from the seeded generator in a fixed order: drop, duplicate, delay, corrupt.

### type Port

```go
type Port struct {

	// WithVCIDFilter

}
```

Port is one endpoint on a virtual bus. It implements [canbus.Transport](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus#Transport), [canbus.Filterer](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus#Filterer), [canbus.Statser](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus#Statser), [canbus.DropCounter](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus#DropCounter), [canbus.Namer](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus#Namer) and [canbus.Capabilitier](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus#Capabilitier); opened [WithXL](#func-withxl), also [canbus.XLTransport](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus#XLTransport).

#### func (Port) Receive

```go
func (p *Port) Receive(ctx context.Context, f *canbus.Frame) error
```

Receive waits for the next CAN or CAN FD frame; CAN XL frames are skipped (use [Port.ReceiveAny](#func-port-receiveany)).

#### func (Port) ReceiveAny

```go
func (p *Port) ReceiveAny(ctx context.Context, f *canbus.Frame, x *canbus.XLFrame) (xl bool, err error)
```

ReceiveAny waits for the next frame of any kind: a CAN or CAN FD frame in f (xl false) or a CAN XL frame in x (xl true), reusing x.Data's storage. With x nil a CAN XL frame is consumed and reported without being copied.

#### func (Port) ReceiveXL

```go
func (p *Port) ReceiveXL(ctx context.Context, x *canbus.XLFrame) error
```

ReceiveXL waits for the next CAN XL frame on a port opened [WithXL](#func-withxl), skipping other frames. x.Data's storage is reused.

#### func (Port) Send

```go
func (p *Port) Send(ctx context.Context, f *canbus.Frame) error
```

Send queues a frame for delivery. A CAN FD frame on a port opened without [WithFD](#func-withfd) fails with [canbus.ErrUnsupported](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus#ErrUnsupported).

#### func (Port) SendXL

```go
func (p *Port) SendXL(ctx context.Context, x *canbus.XLFrame) error
```

SendXL queues a CAN XL frame for delivery, with a copy of its payload. On a port opened without [WithXL](#func-withxl) it fails with [canbus.ErrUnsupported](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus#ErrUnsupported).

### type PortOption

```go
type PortOption func(*Port)
```

PortOption configures a [Port](#type-port).

#### func WithBlocking

```go
func WithBlocking() PortOption
```

WithBlocking makes delivery wait for room in the port's receive queue instead of dropping the frame. The whole bus then waits for the slowest blocking port.

#### func WithFD

```go
func WithFD() PortOption
```

WithFD opens the port for CAN FD frames.

#### func WithFilters

```go
func WithFilters(fs canbus.FilterSet) PortOption
```

WithFilters sets the port's filters, as a SocketCAN socket's kernel filters (see [canbus.FilterSet](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus#FilterSet)).

#### func WithQueueSize

```go
func WithQueueSize(n int) PortOption
```

WithQueueSize sets the port's receive queue capacity (default 1024).

#### func WithRecvOwn

```go
func WithRecvOwn() PortOption
```

WithRecvOwn delivers the port's own transmissions back to it, marked with [canbus.Frame.Echo](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus#Frame.Echo).

#### func WithVCIDFilter

```go
func WithVCIDFilter(vcid, mask uint8) PortOption
```

WithVCIDFilter opens the port for CAN XL frames ([WithXL](#func-withxl)) and receives only those whose VCID matches vcid in the bits of mask, as SocketCAN's CAN\_RAW\_XL\_VCID\_OPTS receive filter.

#### func WithXL

```go
func WithXL() PortOption
```

WithXL opens the port for CAN XL frames ([Port.SendXL](#func-port-sendxl), [Port.ReceiveXL](#func-port-receivexl), [Port.ReceiveAny](#func-port-receiveany)) and, as Linux's CAN\_RAW\_XL\_FRAMES, for CAN FD frames too. It receives CAN XL frames of every VCID.

#### func WithoutLoopback

```go
func WithoutLoopback() PortOption
```

WithoutLoopback stops the port's transmissions from reaching the other ports of this bus (as CAN\_RAW\_LOOPBACK off: in SocketCAN they would still reach other hosts on a real bus).
